newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares end higher, seen firming next week.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares end higher, seen firming next week.

text.p: Brazilian shares closed up 1.65 percent on increased buy orders for Telebras as the market recovered from the shock of an airplane crash on Thursday that killed more than a dozen of bank and company executives, brokers said.
"Market mood improved and investors began to react positively to news that they did not pay attention yesterday. I expect shares to be firmer next week," said a senior trader.
He referred to a Central Bank decision to allow foreign investors to buy convertible debentures through Annex Four regulations, and a reduction in tax on foreign loans.
Analysts also said expectations over the publication next Tuesday of bid specifications for the privatization of Band B cellular services helped to boost market sentiment.
The rules will be subject to public hearings for 15 days and the Communications Ministry expects to start the tender process at the end of this month, according to newspapers.
Preferred shares of Telebras closed up 2.49 percent at 78.20 reais, while the company's common stock rose 2.24 percent to end at 64 reais.
Investors apparently ignored softness in the U.S. stock market and only looked to internal factors, traders added.
Brazil's TAM airline, which had plunged 22.3 percent Thursday following the crash of its Sao Paulo-Rio flight, ended at 54 reais, a rise of over six percent.
Analysts also cited as a big gainer Companhia Siderurgica Nacional (CSN) common shares, which closed up 6.27 percent at 27.10 reais.
The company reported net income of 133.1 million reais in the January-to-September period, against 68.4 million reais for the same period last year.
